g.data-info: Tough outer coat of the seed that protects the embryo; with the tegmen it forms the seed coat.
Two large fleshy seed leaves that store food (mainly starch and protein) for the germinating embryo.
The embryonic shoot, with tiny folded first leaves, lying between the cotyledons.
Short axis joining the plumule and radicle, to which the cotyledons are attached.
The embryonic root; it points toward the micropyle and is the first part to emerge.
Scar on the seed coat where the seed was attached to the fruit wall by its stalk.
Tiny pore in the seed coat near the hilum through which water enters before germination.
